items.question: How does LINE(1st) compare with LINE(2nd) on the Flickr network when the network is very sparse, and what happens as more links are added?
items.gold_answer: When the Flickr network is very sparse, LINE(1st) outperforms LINE(2nd). As the percentage of links increases, LINE(2nd) begins to outperform LINE(1st), showing that second-order proximity is weak in extremely sparse networks but works better when there are enough neighbors.
items.evidence_quote: As we gradually increase the percentage of links, the LINE(2nd) begins to outperform the LINE(1st).

items.question: Under which degree conditions does LINE(2nd) fail to work well on the original Youtube network, and how is this reflected in the grouped results?
items.gold_answer: On the original Youtube network, LINE(2nd) outperforms LINE(1st) except for the first degree group. This indicates that second-order proximity does not work well for nodes with low degree.
items.evidence_quote: In the original network, the LINE(2nd) outperforms LINE(1st) except for thefirst group, which confirms that the second-order proximity does not work well for nodes with a low degree.

items.question: What happens to the performance of LINE(1st) and LINE(2nd) when the embedding dimension d becomes too large?
items.gold_answer: The performance of both LINE(1st) and LINE(2nd) drops when the dimension becomes too large. The passage does not give a specific threshold, only that overly large dimensionality hurts performance.
items.evidence_quote: We can see that the performance of the LINE(1st) or LINE(2nd) drops when the dimension becomes too large.

items.question: How does LINE(2nd) on the reconstructed Youtube network compare with DeepWalk across the degree groups, and what does the reconstructed dense network change?
items.gold_answer: On the reconstructed Youtube network, LINE(2nd) outperforms DeepWalk in all degree groups. The dense reconstructed network also improves the performance of LINE(1st) and LINE(2nd), especially for LINE(2nd), which preserves second-order proximity.
items.evidence_quote: We can also see that the LINE(2nd) model on the reconstructed network outperforms DeepWalk in all the groups.
